subject: On‑prem traffic‑drain + kernel micro‑patch: window proposal and rollback plan
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: SRE Team <sre@finxbank.com>, FinX Security <security@finxbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On‑prem traffic‑drain + kernel micro‑patch: window proposal and rollback plan

Hi team,

We validated the micro‑patch that addresses the CVE in the inference runtime on your private cluster; it requires a short kernel patch on the host VMs and a coordinated network ACL change to drain external traffic off the canary nodes during the operation.

Proposal:
- Window: Thu 31 Jul 2025, 00:30–02:30 UTC (2h)
- Drain plan: 20 minutes to shift traffic off canary slice 1, pause for verification (15m), kernel patch + host reboot on canary nodes (30m), reattach and healthcheck (20m).
- Canary traffic: start at 5% -> 25% after successful verification.
- Rollback: restore VM snapshot (automated) within 15m if healthchecks fail; full rollback target 45m from failure detection.

Attachments: patch-checklist.pdf (steps & prechecks), snapshot-manifest.csv (snapshots/IDs), canary-plan.md (traffic split and metrics).

Ask: please confirm the window and whether FinX Security needs an additional approval step for the host kernel reboot (KMS/HSM key usage) or for us to run the snapshot restore verification in your environment prior to Thu.

Thanks,
Mateo
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@finxbank.com>, FinX Security <security@finxbank.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jul 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem traffic‑drain + kernel micro‑patch: window proposal and rollback plan

Mateo — looks good. A couple of comments from runtime/ops: 
- Add a preflight step to validate evacuation grace: ensure KV cache is flushed and persisted to the prefix cache store (we have a 2‑step flush in patch-checklist).
- Canary rollback path: we should capture and store the host journal logs and container logs to a time‑stamped archive before reboot. Add that to snapshot-manifest.csv as step 0.
- During the 15m verification pause, we should run a lightweight regression (3 golden prompts) against the canary variant to ensure model outputs are within tolerance. canary-plan.md covers this but call it out in the window email to FinX.

I can own the automation for snapshot restore if you want me to run the dry‑run Tuesday morning in your staging cluster.

-karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer

-----

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@finxbank.com>, FinX Security <security@finxbank.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jul 2025 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem traffic‑drain + kernel micro‑patch: window proposal and rollback plan

Adding a few operational notes: 
- We need FinX signoff for the snapshot retention policy: snapshots will be held for 14 days by default (we can extend per request).
- Network ACL change list: we'll apply a temporary deny on the canary public IPs; please confirm if FinX wants the change implemented by your NetOps or if Redwood should push the rule via the private control plane (we have RBAC tokens ready).
- Emergency abort: if the host kernel panics during reboot on >25% of canary hosts, we escalate to emergency unpin (draining the whole slice) and open the bridge. Estimated additional rollback time: ~60–90m.

Monica
Senior Ops Eng

-----

From: SRE Team <sre@finxbank.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: FinX Security <security@finxbank.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem traffic‑drain + kernel micro‑patch: window proposal and rollback plan

Thanks for the plan. A few items from our side before we can approve the Thu window: 
1) KMS flow: we need confirmation that any disk encryption or KMS keys used during reboot do not trigger a rekey operation. Please confirm key usage and whether Redwood will have to present a key handle.
2) Snapshot restore dry‑run: yes, please run the dry‑run in our staging on Tue 29 Jul 10:00–11:30 UTC. Include verification steps and logs.
3) Network change owner: FinX NetOps will apply the ACL change — can you provide the exact CIDR/IP list and an automated rollback playbook for us to run if needed?
4) Can you confirm SLO tolerances for the 2h window? We need token error rate not to exceed 3% sustained.

— FinX SRE (Rahul)
ops@finxbank.com

-----

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: SRE Team <sre@finxbank.com>, FinX Security <security@finxbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 12:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem traffic‑drain + kernel micro‑patch: window proposal and rollback plan

Rahul — thanks, responses inline: 
1) KMS: the patch does not touch disk encryption keys. We will not present any new key handles. Host reboots will use the existing LUKS keys already provisioned; no rekey is expected. I'll get a short KMS confirmation note signed by our security team and attach it to the dry‑run invite.
2) Dry‑run: Karthik will run the automated snapshot restore and we will produce the archived logs (journalctl + container logs) and the verification report. Confirmed Tue 29 Jul 10:00–11:30 UTC.
3) CIDRs: attached in snapshot-manifest.csv under sheet 'net-acl-list' — includes temporary deny entries for canary public IPs. Monica, please keep a rollback playbook snippet (JSON) that FinX NetOps can paste into their system.
4) SLO: we will monitor token error rate and have an automatic fallback to the previous model variant if errors exceed 2.5% for a sustained 5 minutes. If fallback triggers, we will initiate snapshot restore.

Neha — can you review the canary metric set and confirm the three golden prompts for the regression check?

Thanks,
Mateo

-----

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, SRE Team <sre@finxbank.com>, FinX Security <security@finxbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem traffic‑drain + kernel micro‑patch: window proposal and rollback plan

Rahul / FinX SRE — proposed golden prompts below (short deterministic prompts that catch regression blur):
1) "Summarize the last transaction including the last 4 digits and the merchant name." (should be identical to baseline in 99% of cases)
2) "What is the account balance for account ending 1234?" (numeric tolerance +-0.01)
3) "Provide the risk score for transaction id TX-00012345." (categorical match)

We'll run these during the 15m verification pause at 5% load and again at 25% before full rollout. Post‑dry run we'll share the regression artifact.

If FinX NetOps confirms they will own ACL application, please reply and we'll send the final ACL list and the NetOps playbook snippet.

— Neha
QA & Eval Lead
